title: Exclusive Display
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/501538feb0490fddadcb0ca3b601a63146104d57.png)Seven-segment green colour vacuum fluorescent display tube IV-6. Manufactured in the former Soviet Union, 1985. Image source: Mister rf, Wikimedia Commons, Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0 International.

The days-without-incident counter at your factory has become difficult to interpret.

The counter is a single-digit seven-segment display that you bought cheaply in a second-hand hardware store. Each of its seven segments is either off or on, and a digit is shown by turning on the corresponding segments:

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2d85ed1b9a04382a2a7e315b424b9b40e57a0550.png)$\,$ ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/39144f443f531f0384b4a0b52956a2ede5104c93.png)$\,$ ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/09ab2bca429fab9cc70bf14fc7ceb998abb2852e.png)$\,$ ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7e0408ce33bee600afdc42f8bb28f483db1873c8.png)$\,$ ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3d499583fa8f15f695c11220444bef25d8fd29aa.png)$\,$![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/4c821399b26c55be980d1c338e5dd69a2ae7882e.png)$\,$ ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/8dedc57a5243d46daa8cf18d80700a3982018e92.png)$\,$ ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/1b72411e4782033bee260d34d9f90e4da63f1375.png)$\,$ ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a4f6a06ce6983720154d6f9be10e231f001cc3bd.png)$\,$ ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d18fd65ea57182a82f8137930c22947c0f2bdbc7.png)

Every morning, the display is reset so that all segments are off. When a digit is entered into the display, every segment belonging to that digit is flipped: from off to on, or from on to off. This worked just fine as long as the counter only ever needed to show a single digit.

However, thanks to your diligent work with safety protocols, the number of days without incident now routinely reaches two-digit numbers. Since the display has room for only one digit, a two-digit number is entered by typing its two digits one after the other, into the same display. This may well flip a particular segment off again.

The number of days without incident is called the streak length $s$ and satisfies $0\leq s\leq 99$. It is entered without leading $0$s, so a single-digit streak length is entered as one digit.

Given the state of the display after the streak length has been entered, determine which values of $s$ could have produced it.

## Input

The input consists of:

- $7$ lines, each with $4$ characters, each character being either "`.`" or "`#`".

The input describes a possible state of the seven-segment display, with two characters used for each of the seven segments. Each segment can be off or on, shown as "`..`" or "`##`", respectively, either horizontally or vertically. The parts of the input that don't correspond to segments are always shown as "`.`" for readability.

## Output

Output the possible streak lengths, without leading $0$s. If there is more than one possible streak length, report all of them in sorted order. If no streak length could have resulted in the input display, output "`impossible`".
